text:
maria: FYI posting the Lyra postmortem follow-ups — isolation bug during customer on‑prem VPC peering caused a dedicated pool failover and partial tenant isolation. I pulled the key action items below and assigned tentative owners.

aj: Quick summary + owners/timeline?

maria: TL;DR — peering route flaps + asymmetric SNAT from customer NAT led to session staleness. Two main remediations: (1) fix peering route filtering + add health checks for onprem endpoints, and (2) add a defensive connection drain/eviction path in the runtime when peer route changes are detected.

kevin: I can own the peering route filter change (infra side). Target: configuration PR by Tue EOD, deployment Wed midnight maintenance window. Need +2h maintenance window and a rollback play.

maria: noted. Kevin -> INF-4876 created and added to "peering-stability" sprint.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: new ticket created INF-4876 by kevin.

aj: Runtime eviction path — who? And test coverage?

kevin: runtime folks will need to coordinate; leaving to @devex for test harness + @maria for priority.

devex: I can write an end-to-end harness to simulate asymmetric SNAT + route flaps. ETA mock harness by Thu. Will add a regression test that replays the packet/route sequence.

maria: Assigned runtime work INF-4877 to "kevin"? wait, reassign to @kevin-runtime? Actually runtime owner is kevin (same person), INF-4877 created for runtime eviction + metric hooks.

aj: Please include success criteria: 1) no tenant isolation after synthetic route flap for 5m, 2) eviction + sticky-cache invalidation within 10s of route change, 3) automated regression test added to nightly.

maria: Adding success criteria to both tickets.

kevin: For the infra change I'll surface the minimal iptables rule we want in the PR; quick snippet for reviewers:

```
# reject asymmetrically NATed return path from customer on peering CIDR
iptables -A INPUT -s <customer-peering-cidr> -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -s <customer-peering-cidr> -j DROP
```

kevin: Note: we'll gate the DROP behind an allowlist during canary.

maria: Documentation: I added a postmortem doc and a checklist (https://redwood.infra/docs/postmortems/lyra-2024) with links to INF-4876/4877 and a short runbook for oncall.

aj: Can we schedule a 30m sync to hand off the infra and runtime tickets to the sprint? If so, propose Thu 11am PT.

kevin: Thu 11am PT works. I'll prepare the PR diff + staged canary plan.

devex: I'll bring the harness and the initial failing regression case so SRE can validate.

maria: Owners and timelines:
- kevin: INF-4876 infra peering rules -> PR Tue EOD, deploy Wed midnight (2h window)
- kevin: INF-4877 runtime eviction + metrics -> prototype Wed, PR Fri
- devex: harness + regression tests -> Thu AM, add to nightly -> Fri
- maria: postmortem doc + runbook updates -> done; will follow up on customer comms by EOD Mon.

sre-oncall: 👍 will monitor the canary and stand by for rollback.

aj: I'll add a recurring check in the incident pattern tracker to surface similar VPC peering flaps monthly (INF-4900).

maria: One more: export of recent tenant evictions and KV cache invalidations attached to INF-4877 for post-change comparison.

kevin: Agreed. I'll add the logs query to the runtime PR template.

maria: thanks all — proceeding to create the sprint cards and invite owners for Thu sync. If anyone needs to reassign, ping me in-thread. :thumbsup:
